outputs.question: How do I initiate Rework for a Job?

input.question: how do i initiate rework for a job

excerpts.title: Initiate Job Rework
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Authorized business writers can create Rework for a completed Production Job. Open the Job in Production and select Create Rework. Choose a Reason, describe Rework Scope / Work Required, enter Intake / Return Date, then select Create Rework. The Job must be complete, unarchived and have no active Rework cycle. Only one Rework cycle can be active at a time. Rework remains on the same canonical Job and preserves original Production status and dates. Scope is a whole-Job description, not structured piece or Color Plate tracking.

excerpts.title: Production Rework lifecycle and requirements
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Rework belongs to an existing canonical Production Job. Only one active Rework is allowed; eligible Job states and the actual Create Rework action remain authoritative. TenOps models Rework as a lifecycle belonging to one canonical commercial Production Job. The Job number, customer, commercial values, documents, attachments, Purchase Orders, Transmittals, and Job Updates remain job-scoped. The original lifecycle remains on jobs; Rework never overwrites its status or planned dates. Only one Rework can be active for a Job, while completed and cancelled cycles remain historical. outputs.question: How do I filter Manpower Reporting by Job?

input.question: how do i filter manpower reporting by job

excerpts.title: Filter Manpower Reporting by Job
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Employees with business-write access can filter labor by Production Job. Open Reporting → Manpower Reporting, then choose the Job in Job labor review. Use Clear job filter or All reporting groups to reset. After selecting a Job, Product Category filter narrows products. Analytics use the selected reporting period; reporting rows are loaded complete groups with all their dates. Search and filters are not exhaustive until all available history is loaded. Read-only accounts cannot change the current Job labor review selector, but can use Search manpower or open a Job’s Current Hours link from Production.

excerpts.title: Manpower Reporting work identity and filters
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Job dropdown filtering uses business-write-gated controls in the released UI. Read-only accounts retain search/authorized deep-link review. Reporting groups are not Jobs. Manpower Reporting records labor by reporting group, work date, worker, task, work identity, AM hours, PM hours, notes, and attribution. Persistent reporting groups organize entry and review; they are not jobs. Work identity is either a Production job or temporary label, never both. Workers and tasks are stable references with display order and active state. Historical references are deactivated rather than deleted. Total hours derive from AM plus PM and are not stored. Client-side search covers group, date, worker, task, job name/number, temporary label, notes, and entered-by. Search changes displayed rows and totals without changing persistence or ordering. outputs.question: How do I edit an existing customer?

input.question: how do i edit an existing customer

excerpts.title: Edit a saved customer’s details
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Open Toolbox → Resources → Contacts. Search for the beginning of the customer’s company name, then select the company name to open Customer Inspector. Edit Customer / Company Name, or expand Additional Information (Optional) to edit Contact Name, Phone Number or Email Address. Choose Save Changes. Lead/Admin access is required to edit a saved customer; read-only accounts cannot save changes. Saved changes apply to future selections. Existing Jobs and Proposals keep their captured information.

excerpts.title: Shared Contacts and Customer Inspector
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Saved customer editing requires existing business-write and customer-detail editing permissions. Future selections use updated directory values; existing Jobs/issued Proposals retain their captured values. Customer search and Linked Jobs are available separately with operational-read access. outputs.question: How do I create a group conversation?

input.question: how do i create a group conversation

excerpts.title: Create a group conversation
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Open Messaging from the app header. Choose New group, enter a group name, select at least one other participant, then choose Create group. Only the creator can rename the group or add/remove participants. Current members share the full history; removed members lose access. Previously signed attachment links may remain usable for up to ten minutes.

excerpts.title: Messaging groups, personal DMs and conversation privacy
excerpts.guidance: Account decision: available. Employees can create creator-managed groups, send messages and attachments, and reply within an authorized conversation. Adding a third person to an existing personal DM is not supported: create a separate group; old DM history stays private and is not copied. A dedicated Share Job control is not verified; do not invent it. Official TenOps system notices retain separate authority. TenBot receives no employee Messaging records. - My Work and Inbox are participant/private domains. Task estimated effort supports workload views; attachments and typing/Realtime authorization preserve private boundaries.
